definitions.explanation: The most important or central element of something — the part that holds everything together. Originally referred to the rivet of a folding fan.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}はチームの{要|かなめ}だ。
examples.english: He is the linchpin of the team.

examples.japanese: {交渉|こうしょう}の{要|かなめ}は{信頼関係|しんらいかんけい}だ。
examples.english: The key to negotiation is a relationship of trust.

examples.japanese: {防衛|ぼうえい}の{要|かなめ}となる{地域|ちいき}を{確保|かくほ}しなければならない。
examples.english: We must secure the region that serves as the linchpin of defense.

notes:
The crucial element that everything depends on. Originally the rivet ({要|かなめ}) of a folding fan ({扇|おうぎ}) — the small pin at the base that holds all the blades together. Without it, the fan falls apart, hence the figurative meaning.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- チームの{要|かなめ} — linchpin of the team
- {組織|そしき}の{要|かなめ} — the key person/element of an organization
- {防衛|ぼうえい}の{要|かなめ} — linchpin of defense
- {要|かなめ}となる — to serve as the key element
- {扇|おうぎ}の{要|かなめ} — the pivot of a fan (also figurative: the central hub)

ETYMOLOGY:
From the rivet ({要|かなめ}) of a folding fan. The metaphor of a small but essential component holding a larger structure together is the core of this word's meaning.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {要|よう} — necessity, need (same kanji, on'yomi reading, different nuance)
- {中心|ちゅうしん} — center, core (more neutral, less emphasis on indispensability)
- {柱|はしら} — pillar (similar metaphor of structural support)

AS A NAME:
{要|かなめ} is also used as a given name (for both genders), suggesting someone essential or pivotal.
